subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Straw Man Fallacy
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Straw Man Fallacy.

hook.text: "We should reduce sugar in school lunches." "So you want to starve our children?" That's a straw man.

buildup.text: A straw man distorts an opponent's argument into a weaker version, then attacks the distortion.

discovery.text: It works by substituting an extreme caricature for the real position. The audience may not notice the swap.

twist.text: It's often unintentional. People genuinely misrepresent positions they don't fully understand.

climax.text: The steel man is the antidote: state the opponent's best argument before responding to it.

punchline.text: Fight the real argument, not its shadow.

quiz.question: What is a straw man fallacy?
options: Distorting an argument to make it easier to attack
Attacking the strongest version of an argument

details.summary: A straw man fallacy misrepresents an opponent's argument to make it easier to attack. Instead of engaging the actual position, you create a weaker or more extreme version and then refute that. It is extremely common in political debates and online arguments.
details.whyItMatters: Straw man arguments feel persuasive because they do refute something. Recognizing the trick keeps you from being misled by apparent victories over positions nobody holds.
takeaways: A straw man distorts the opponent's actual argument
The distorted version is easier to attack but not the real position
Always verify you are engaging the strongest version of any argument

faq.question: How do you detect a straw man argument?
faq.answer: Check whether the refuted position is actually what the opponent claimed. If the rebuttal addresses an exaggerated, simplified, or different version of the original argument, it is a straw man. Ask: would the original speaker agree that this is what they said? If not, it is a straw man.

faq.question: What is the opposite of a straw man?
faq.answer: A steel man. Steel-manning means reconstructing your opponent's argument in its strongest possible form before engaging it. If you can refute the strongest version, your rebuttal is genuinely powerful. Steel-manning also promotes intellectual honesty and productive disagreement.
